purpose: Trace current subgroups and roles to their recorded ISCO, ESCO, O*NET or specialist-framework evidence without asserting that source presence proves Nigerian demand or learner competence.
limitations: The base role library source field is not itself a complete citation. Exact ESCO evidence requires a valid esco_code and the corresponding local ESCO record; exact O*NET evidence requires a recorded O*NET code/profile.
Specialist overlay provenance identifies the framework and evidence description, but it does not prove Nigerian vacancy volume or licensing.
A subgroup source anchor establishes a grouping rationale; it does not prove that every role in the subgroup belongs there without role-level review.

Roles whose ISCO sub-major has no matching subgroup are intentionally exposed through the direct domain-to-role fallback. This is not an invented subgroup assignment and is not counted as a structural failure.
An O*NET work profile is a global/US proxy and is not a Nigerian hiring requirement.

A role with no stored code is matched to O*NET 31.0 only when its exact current role title matches an O*NET occupation title; the audit records that match and does not alter the role library automatically.

onet_title_match.title: Cytogenetic Technologists
onet_title_match.description: Analyze chromosomes or chromosome segments found in biological specimens, such as amniotic fluids, bone marrow, solid tumors, and blood to aid in the study, diagnosis, classification, or treatment of inherited or acquired genetic diseases. Conduct analyses through classical cytogenetic, fluorescent in situ hybridization (FISH) or array comparative genome hybridization (aCGH) techniques.

onet_title_match.title: Cytotechnologists
onet_title_match.description: Stain, mount, and study cells to detect evidence of cancer, hormonal abnormalities, and other pathological conditions following established standards and practices.

onet_title_match.title: Dermatologists
onet_title_match.description: Diagnose and treat diseases relating to the skin, hair, and nails. May perform both medical and dermatological surgery functions.

onet_title_match.title: Emergency Medical Technicians
onet_title_match.description: Assess injuries and illnesses and administer basic emergency medical care. May transport injured or sick persons to medical facilities.

onet_title_match.title: Emergency Medicine Physicians
onet_title_match.description: Make immediate medical decisions and act to prevent death or further disability. Provide immediate recognition, evaluation, care, stabilization, and disposition of patients. May direct emergency medical staff in an emergency department.

onet_title_match.title: Family Medicine Physicians
onet_title_match.description: Diagnose, treat, and provide preventive care to individuals and families across the lifespan. May refer patients to specialists when needed for further diagnosis or treatment.

onet_title_match.title: General Internal Medicine Physicians
onet_title_match.description: Diagnose and provide nonsurgical treatment for a wide range of diseases and injuries of internal organ systems. Provide care mainly for adults and adolescents, and are based primarily in an outpatient care setting.

onet_title_match.title: Genetic Counselors
onet_title_match.description: Assess individual or family risk for a variety of inherited conditions, such as genetic disorders and birth defects. Provide information to other healthcare providers or to individuals and families concerned with the risk of inherited conditions. Advise individuals and families to support informed decisionmaking and coping methods for those at risk. May help conduct research related to genetic conditions or genetic counseling.

onet_title_match.title: Histology Technicians
onet_title_match.description: Prepare histological slides from tissue sections for microscopic examination and diagnosis by pathologists. May assist with research studies.

onet_title_match.title: Histotechnologists
onet_title_match.description: Apply knowledge of health and disease causes to evaluate new laboratory techniques and procedures to examine tissue samples. Process and prepare histological slides from tissue sections for microscopic examination and diagnosis by pathologists. May solve technical or instrument problems or assist with research studies.

onet_title_match.title: Hospitalists
onet_title_match.description: Provide inpatient care predominantly in settings such as medical wards, acute care units, intensive care units, rehabilitation centers, or emergency rooms. Manage and coordinate patient care throughout treatment.

onet_title_match.title: Medical Appliance Technicians
onet_title_match.description: Construct, maintain, or repair medical supportive devices such as braces, orthotics and prosthetic devices, joints, arch supports, and other surgical and medical appliances.

onet_title_match.title: Medical and Clinical Laboratory Technologists
onet_title_match.description: Perform complex medical laboratory tests for diagnosis, treatment, and prevention of disease. May train or supervise staff.

onet_title_match.title: Midwives
onet_title_match.description: Provide prenatal care and childbirth assistance.

onet_title_match.title: Neurologists
onet_title_match.description: Diagnose, manage, and treat disorders and diseases of the brain, spinal cord, and peripheral nerves, with a primarily nonsurgical focus.

onet_title_match.title: Nurse Practitioners
onet_title_match.description: Diagnose and treat acute, episodic, or chronic illness, independently or as part of a healthcare team. May focus on health promotion and disease prevention. May order, perform, or interpret diagnostic tests such as lab work and x rays. May prescribe medication. Must be registered nurses who have specialized graduate education.

onet_title_match.title: Obstetricians and Gynecologists
onet_title_match.description: Provide medical care related to pregnancy or childbirth. Diagnose, treat, and help prevent diseases of women, particularly those affecting the reproductive system. May also provide general care to women. May perform both medical and gynecological surgery functions.

onet_title_match.title: Ophthalmic Laboratory Technicians
onet_title_match.description: Cut, grind, and polish eyeglasses, contact lenses, or other precision optical elements. Assemble and mount lenses into frames or process other optical elements. Includes precision lens polishers or grinders, centerer-edgers, and lens mounters.

onet_title_match.title: Ophthalmologists, Except Pediatric
onet_title_match.description: Diagnose and perform surgery to treat and help prevent disorders and diseases of the eye. May also provide vision services for treatment including glasses and contacts.

onet_title_match.title: Oral and Maxillofacial Surgeons
onet_title_match.description: Perform surgery and related procedures on the hard and soft tissues of the oral and maxillofacial regions to treat diseases, injuries, or defects. May diagnose problems of the oral and maxillofacial regions. May perform surgery to improve function or appearance.

onet_title_match.title: Orthopedic Surgeons, Except Pediatric
onet_title_match.description: Diagnose and perform surgery to treat and prevent rheumatic and other diseases in the musculoskeletal system.

onet_title_match.title: Orthotists and Prosthetists
onet_title_match.description: Design, measure, fit, and adapt orthopedic braces, appliances or prostheses, such as limbs or facial parts for patients with disabling conditions.

onet_title_match.title: Pediatric Surgeons
onet_title_match.description: Diagnose and perform surgery to treat fetal abnormalities and birth defects, diseases, and injuries in fetuses, premature and newborn infants, children, and adolescents. Includes all pediatric surgical specialties and subspecialties.

onet_title_match.title: Pediatricians, General
onet_title_match.description: Diagnose, treat, and help prevent diseases and injuries in children. May refer patients to specialists for further diagnosis or treatment, as needed.

onet_title_match.title: Physical Medicine and Rehabilitation Physicians
onet_title_match.description: Diagnose and treat disorders requiring physiotherapy to provide physical, mental, and occupational rehabilitation.

onet_title_match.title: Physicians, Pathologists
onet_title_match.description: Diagnose diseases and conduct lab tests using organs, body tissues, and fluids. Includes medical examiners.

onet_title_match.title: Preventive Medicine Physicians
onet_title_match.description: Apply knowledge of general preventive medicine and public health issues to promote health care to groups or individuals, and aid in the prevention or reduction of risk of disease, injury, disability, or death. May practice population-based medicine or diagnose and treat patients in the context of clinical health promotion and disease prevention.

onet_title_match.title: Psychiatrists
onet_title_match.description: Diagnose, treat, and help prevent mental disorders.

onet_title_match.title: Radiologists
onet_title_match.description: Diagnose and treat diseases and injuries using medical imaging techniques, such as x rays, magnetic resonance imaging (MRI), nuclear medicine, and ultrasounds. May perform minimally invasive medical procedures and tests.

onet_title_match.title: Sports Medicine Physicians
onet_title_match.description: Diagnose, treat, and help prevent injuries that occur during sporting events, athletic training, and physical activities.

onet_title_match.title: Surgeons, All Other
onet_title_match.description: All surgeons not listed separately.

onet_title_match.title: Surgical Assistants
onet_title_match.description: Assist in operations, under the supervision of surgeons. May, in accordance with state laws, help surgeons to make incisions and close surgical sites, manipulate or remove tissues, implant surgical devices or drains, suction the surgical site, place catheters, clamp or cauterize vessels or tissue, and apply dressings to surgical site.

onet_title_match.title: Urologists
onet_title_match.description: Diagnose, treat, and help prevent benign and malignant medical and surgical disorders of the genitourinary system and the renal glands.

work_profile_source_links.label: Health Information Technologists and Medical Registrars

onet_title_match.title: Acute Care Nurses
onet_title_match.description: Provide advanced nursing care for patients with acute conditions such as heart attacks, respiratory distress syndrome, or shock. May care for pre- and post-operative patients or perform advanced, invasive diagnostic or therapeutic procedures.

onet_title_match.title: Advanced Practice Psychiatric Nurses
onet_title_match.description: Assess, diagnose, and treat individuals and families with mental health or substance use disorders or the potential for such disorders. Apply therapeutic activities, including the prescription of medication, per state regulations, and the administration of psychotherapy.

onet_title_match.title: Clinical Nurse Specialists
onet_title_match.description: Direct nursing staff in the provision of patient care in a clinical practice setting, such as a hospital, hospice, clinic, or home. Ensure adherence to established clinical policies, protocols, regulations, and standards.

onet_title_match.title: Critical Care Nurses
onet_title_match.description: Provide specialized nursing care for patients in critical or coronary care units.

onet_title_match.title: Home Health Aides
onet_title_match.description: Monitor the health status of an individual with disabilities or illness, and address their health-related needs, such as changing bandages, dressing wounds, or administering medication. Work is performed under the direction of offsite or intermittent onsite licensed nursing staff. Provide assistance with routine healthcare tasks or activities of daily living, such as feeding, bathing, toileting, or ambulation. May also help with tasks such as preparing meals, doing light housekeeping, and doing laundry depending on the patient's abilities.

roles.role_key: D024|Licensed Practical and Licensed Vocational Nurses
roles.role_name: Licensed Practical and Licensed Vocational Nurses

onet_title_match.title: Licensed Practical and Licensed Vocational Nurses
onet_title_match.description: Care for ill, injured, or convalescing patients or persons with disabilities in hospitals, nursing homes, clinics, private homes, group homes, and similar institutions. May work under the supervision of a registered nurse. Licensing required.

work_profile_source_links.label: Licensed Practical and Licensed Vocational Nurses

onet_title_match.title: Medical Assistants
onet_title_match.description: Perform administrative and certain clinical duties under the direction of a physician. Administrative duties may include scheduling appointments, maintaining medical records, billing, and coding information for insurance purposes. Clinical duties may include taking and recording vital signs and medical histories, preparing patients for examination, drawing blood, and administering medications as directed by physician.

onet_title_match.title: Nurse Anesthetists
onet_title_match.description: Administer anesthesia, monitor patient's vital signs, and oversee patient recovery from anesthesia. May assist anesthesiologists, surgeons, other physicians, or dentists. Must be registered nurses who have specialized graduate education.

onet_title_match.title: Nurse Midwives
onet_title_match.description: Diagnose and coordinate all aspects of the birthing process, either independently or as part of a healthcare team. May provide well-woman gynecological care. Must have specialized, graduate nursing education.

onet_title_match.title: Nursing Assistants
onet_title_match.description: Provide or assist with basic care or support under the direction of onsite licensed nursing staff. Perform duties such as monitoring of health status, feeding, bathing, dressing, grooming, toileting, or ambulation of patients in a health or nursing facility. May include medication administration and other health-related tasks. Includes nursing care attendants, nursing aides, and nursing attendants.

work_profile_source_links.label: World Economic Forum Future of Jobs 2025

onet_title_match.title: Orderlies
onet_title_match.description: Transport patients to areas such as operating rooms or x-ray rooms using wheelchairs, stretchers, or moveable beds. May maintain stocks of supplies or clean and transport equipment. Psychiatric orderlies are included in Psychiatric Aides.

onet_title_match.title: Patient Representatives
onet_title_match.description: Assist patients in obtaining services, understanding policies and making health care decisions.

onet_title_match.title: Personal Care Aides
onet_title_match.description: Provide personalized assistance to individuals with disabilities or illness who require help with personal care and activities of daily living support (e.g., feeding, bathing, dressing, grooming, toileting, and ambulation). May also provide help with tasks such as preparing meals, doing light housekeeping, and doing laundry. Work is performed in various settings depending on the needs of the care recipient and may include locations such as their home, place of work, out in the community, or at a daytime nonresidential facility.

work_profile_source_links.label: World Economic Forum Future of Jobs 2025

onet_title_match.title: Phlebotomists
onet_title_match.description: Draw blood for tests, transfusions, donations, or research. May explain the procedure to patients and assist in the recovery of patients with adverse reactions.

onet_title_match.title: Psychiatric Aides
onet_title_match.description: Assist mentally impaired or emotionally disturbed patients, working under direction of nursing and medical staff. May assist with daily living activities, lead patients in educational and recreational activities, or accompany patients to and from examinations and treatments. May restrain violent patients. Includes psychiatric orderlies.

onet_title_match.title: Registered Nurses
onet_title_match.description: Assess patient health problems and needs, develop and implement nursing care plans, and maintain medical records. Administer nursing care to ill, injured, convalescent, or disabled patients. May advise patients on health maintenance and disease prevention or provide case management. Licensing or registration required.
